function: Learned LEO satellite-user matching (HGPAN) and beamforming vectors (IGEAN) maximizing secrecy rate against eavesdroppers in a multi-satellite downlink (pp. 3, 5).
system: LEO satellites with Nt = 4 beamforming antennas, M = 200, single-antenna users and eavesdroppers, 11.7 GHz (Ku band), no RIS (p. 8, Table I).
method: Heterogeneous graph attention network HGPAN (supervised, cross-entropy on matching labels from many-to-many matching) plus isomorphic GNN IGEAN (unsupervised, secrecy-rate loss) (pp. 6-8).
data_channel: Own simulator: free-space path loss with Doppler and array response (Eq. 1), random node positions, 10000 samples split 9:1:1; no standard or measured channel (pp. 3, 8).
test_conditions: Same simulator for training and testing (9:1:1 split); sweeps of power, users, satellites, altitude, antennas, CSI error; no train-in-one, test-in-another setting stated (pp. 8-12).
baselines: Non-learned: Con-opt (many-to-many matching plus convex optimization), genetic algorithm, ant colony. Learned: DNN, GAT, fully connected layer, and their combinations such as DDNN, DNN-GAT (p. 8).
metrics: Sum secrecy rate, accuracy (achievable over optimal secrecy rate), computation time, beam alignment rho, communication rate, training and validation loss (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Big-O orders for HGPAN (p. 7) and IGEAN (p. 8); computation times in Fig. 7: G-MSC-SC 7.29 s, Con-opt 21.73 s (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 3: "considering the free-space path loss in the MSC system, the channel model of the LEO satellite user is expressed as"; custom free-space and Doppler model (Eq. 1), with no 3GPP TR 38.811 or 38.901, other standard model or measured data mentioned.
q2_support: p. 8: "contains the training, validation, and test sets in the ratio 9:1:1"; the sweeps over users, satellites, altitude and CSI error (pp. 10-12) are not stated to test a model trained under other conditions, and Fig. 9 plots convergence per epoch for each setting.
q3_support: p. 10: "the accuracy of the algorithm is defined as the ratio of the achievable secrecy rate to the average optimal secrecy rate"; Fig. 8 compares the proposed method with Con-opt, GA and Ant (non-learned) and DNN, GAT and FL schemes (learned, listed on p. 8).
q4_support: p. 8: "Its total computational complexity is O"; the HGPAN order is on p. 7 ("The total complexity of HGPAN") and computation times are in Fig. 7 (p. 10).
q5_support: p. 8: "The dataset of G-MSC-SC is 10000"; the data are self-generated by simulation, and no code or data link, DOI or public dataset is given.
notes: Area 6: learned beam control and satellite-user matching in LEO links; a learned physical-layer decision (beamforming) jointly with matching passes above_phy, and secrecy-rate beamforming is not authentication. Table I (p. 8): 11.7 GHz, Nt=4, M=200, N=30, E=30. Ablation variants in Fig. 12 (p. 12) are not counted as baselines. Channel follows refs [36], [37] and is custom.
